newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish police break up Islamist protesters.
newsitem.headline: Turkish police break up Islamist protesters.

text.p: Turkish police firing water cannon from armoured cars broke up a demonstration by thousands of Islamists in the centre of the capital on Tuesday, witnesses said.
They said the Islamists fled a police charge outside the education ministry after hours of rowdy protests against plans to extend secularist school education.

Around 100 policemen wielding batons chased Islamists up a main street. At least two people received head wounds but it was not clear whether they were protesters or undercover members of the security forces.
Earlier, police arrested 55 people as they tried to approach the headquarters of the secularist military, state-run Anatolian news agency said.
Witnesses estimated a crowd of around 6,000 Islamists had marched through the city chanting slogans against the government of Prime Minster Mesut Yilmaz, a secularist.
Yilmaz took office in June after Islamist predecessor Necmettin Erbakan stepped down under pressure from the secularist army.
